profile.name: Adnan Bashir
profile.description: Adnan Bashir — AI and time-series researcher, cybersecurity educator, and PhD candidate. Teaching and research at the intersection of intelligence, security, and visual exploration.

hero.intro: I’m Adnan Bashir. I study how machines learn from changing data, teach cybersecurity, and build tools that make complex ideas visible.

about.heading:
Between intelligence,
security, and curiosity.
about.lead: My work connects machine learning, time-series analysis, and cybersecurity education.
about.secondary: I’m interested in the moments when data changes—and how we can help people understand what that change means.
about.note: I bring research into the classroom through numerical examples and small, inspectable experiments. My work moves between statistical methods, software tools, and the visual language we use to explain them.

items.title: SegStream
items.subtitle: Time-series segmentation & state discovery
items.description: Investigating how to divide a multivariate time series into meaningful segments and identify the states within it. The work brings boundary detection and state discovery into a shared experimental workflow.

notes.heading: The question
notes.text: Where does one behavior end, and another begin?

notes.heading: The approach
notes.text: Inspect neighboring windows, score potential boundaries, and explore how segments relate to recurring states.

items.title: DRUM-Ext
items.subtitle: Window comparisons & boundary scoring
items.description: Exploring how comparisons between neighboring windows reveal changes in a signal. Experiments examine window size, feature behavior, and boundary scores across different datasets.

notes.heading: What I examine
notes.text: The influence of window length, feature changes, and the tolerance used to match detected boundaries.

notes.heading: Why it matters
notes.text: A boundary should reflect a change in the underlying behavior, with evidence that can be inspected.

items.title: Statistical change detection
items.subtitle: From test statistics to interpretable experiments
items.description: Studying nearest-neighbor two-sample tests and ISSD-related methods to understand the evidence behind a detected change. Numerical walkthroughs and visual experiments make assumptions and test behavior easier to inspect.

notes.heading: The question
notes.text: Do two windows contain evidence of the same distribution?

notes.heading: The explanation
notes.text: Work through the statistic, its null behavior, and what changes under an alternative hypothesis.

teaching.heading:
Make it clear.
Then go deeper.
teaching.intro: I use concrete examples, numerical walkthroughs, and interactive experiments to help students move from intuition to understanding.

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: How do we represent knowledge, search for solutions, reason under uncertainty, and learn from data?
topics: Machine learning within the broader field of AI

courses.name: Computer Networks
courses.description: What happens between sending a message and receiving it? Follow data through protocols, networks, and the Internet.
topics: Links, transmission, and network security foundations

exploration.heading: Ideas you can see.
paragraphs: Alongside research and teaching, I build interactive visualizations: tools for inspecting time-series boundaries, exploring statistical tests, and explaining the mathematics behind machine learning.
Changing a parameter should reveal something. A visualization becomes useful when it helps us ask a better question.

featured.heading:
From an idea
to something you can use.
featured.intro: Research tools, small utilities, and creative experiments. These are a few of the things I’ve built along the way.

gallery.intro: A collection of tools for measuring, learning, exploring, and creating. Open a project and try it for yourself.

projects.name: RAFTAR
projects.description: A browser speed test with an instrument-style dashboard for download speed, upload speed, and latency.
projects.features: Analog and digital gauges · configurable appearance · connection measurements

projects.name: ZARB
projects.description: Tap along with a rhythm to estimate its tempo. Follow BPM, the running average, and the range of your taps through a customizable gauge.
projects.features: Tap tempo · session log · minimum and maximum BPM
projects.note: A tap-tempo tool; it does not analyze uploaded audio.

projects.name: Boundary & State Lab
projects.description: Explore time-series boundaries and states through an interactive SegStream workspace with embedded datasets and saved analysis.
projects.features: Signal inspection · window comparisons · boundary and state exploration
projects.note: Includes the bundled research data. Initial loading may take a moment.

projects.name: NET Practice Simulator
projects.description: Practice Mathematics, Physics, and English with a configurable exam, timed sections, worked explanations, and topic-level results.
projects.features: Five difficulty levels · saved attempts · grading and review · exports
projects.note: Practice material. Internet is needed to load the mathematics renderer.

projects.name: Urdu Word Cloud
projects.description: An evolving composition of Urdu expressions, shaped by script, scale, and color. Explore a different side of my work through typography.
projects.features: Urdu font choices · six color palettes · animated word layout

projects.name: Enterprise Workspace
projects.description: A browser-based operations workspace connecting tasks, people, planning, approvals, and reporting in one interface.
projects.features: Task workflows · monthly planning · audit log · theme customization
projects.note: Interactive prototype with demonstration records stored in your browser.

projects.name: Cantt Events
projects.description: An events-management prototype combining hall bookings, a fleet map, alerts, and operational reports.
projects.features: Booking calendar · simulated fleet tracking · map themes · PDF reports
projects.note: Demonstration fleet data. Maps and chart libraries require internet.

projects.name: Tilt Scale
projects.description: Explore the relationship between tilt and balance using a phone’s motion sensor, a simple beam, and a known calibration weight.
projects.features: Guided setup · zeroing · calibration · saved readings
projects.note: Best on a compatible phone over HTTPS; requires sensor permission and a physical setup.
